How this calculation works
  1. The target In/Ga ratio fixes the group-III fractions. Vegard interpolation determines As/P for lattice matching at the XRD temperature.
  2. The model's target transition energy is shifted to match your measured reference PL. This constant energy offset is used locally for the grown layer; it is not a fitted spectrometer wavelength calibration.
  3. The selected bulk or strain-corrected direct Γ gap is fitted with symmetric 004 XRD. XRD always retains coherent elastic strain. With bandgap strain enabled, hydrostatic shifts and HH/LH mixing are included. Twenty-five starts seek distinct solutions. No-solution and multiple-solution cases stop recommendations.
  4. The known incorporated III rate establishes the total rate. Desired partial rates set source-temperature corrections through the logarithmic calibration slopes.
  5. The provisional As incorporation model requests BEPnew/BEPold = [(ytargetRtarget)/(ycurrentRcurrent)]1/n. The measured fifth-degree curve is then inverted within its calibrated range. P stays fixed; its measured curve is also available in the converter.
  6. Each percentage interpolates the temperature or valve position between the current setting and the full correction.

Scope: coherent, bulk-like InGaAsP on InP (001), direct band-edge emission, 250–350 K measurement temperatures. Not a quantum-well or partial-relaxation model. Exact source hardware limits and settling times are not modeled.

Composition and prediction accuracy depend on the material model, the reference layer and incorporation assumptions. A single PL anchor fixes a local offset, not the composition slopes. Displayed uncertainty propagates current PL/XRD measurement errors only; reference, source calibration and model uncertainties are excluded.

Parameter basis: Minch et al. (1999); Vurgaftman et al. (2001). Python core adapted from your supplied composition model. This tuner is not an exact reproduction of MyCAL_v3.vi.
